static_traits.name: Lin Ke
static_traits.family_status: Lives with family, relatively high family support
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with classmates due to pessimism and self-criticism; has not yet discussed academic difficulties and negative thoughts with family
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, acceptable logic, hesitant tone with Anxiety; able to engage in discussion, willing to try new approaches

basic_info.main_problem: Despite returning to school to pursue a degree, I perform poorly in many courses, and have developed a sense of inadequacy and pessimism about academic performance and future job prospects.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to address these problems before they further affect mental health (handling Declining academic performance and negative thoughts about future employment).
growth_experiences: Receiving below-Anticipation grades since the start of this semester has triggered and worsened Self-doubt and pessimism; Anxiety and worry are especially likely around assignment and exam feedback, while needing to balance academics with other responsibilities, pressure has risen significantly.

In several past courses, the client expected to fail but ultimately achieved Good grades; however the client tends to view these successes as 'exceptions' and has not yet integrated them as evidence of self-efficacy.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough/not good enough
I may never find a decent Work

special_situations.event: Receiving below-Anticipation scores on assignments or exams
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If grades are not high, it means I am not smart enough and the future has no prospects
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to improve study habits and seeking academic support
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It's over, I may not be able to find Work

special_situations.event: Before grades are announced or just at the moment of Receiving grades
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once there is one poor performance, it will continue to be poor afterwards
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to improve study habits and seeking academic support, but still worrying repeatedly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time I will definitely do badly on the exam; the outcome will be terrible

special_situations.event: Interacting with classmates, comparing academic performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not like my peers, I do not deserve to be accepted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing in front of classmates, reducing interaction to avoid comparison
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all better than me, I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: Recalling good grades achieved in the past
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only sustained, comprehensive success counts as truly capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores positive evidence and treats success as an 'exception'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those successes do not count, they cannot prove I am capable

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and supported in academics and career, and to be accepted
core_conflict.fear: Worries about making others (family/peers) worry or look down on him
defense_goal: Maintains a certain distance to preserve a sense of safety and avoid being evaluated or burdening others

object_relations.self_representation: A student who is not good enough and prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Classmates are others who are more outstanding and may judge her

object_relations.self_representation: A child who does not want to trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Family members are others who will worry and may look down on her

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks whether she has shared academic difficulties with family and sought support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes expressing difficulties will make family worry or look down on them (projecting their own shame and worry onto others' reactions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Hesitant, cautious tone, responding with 'I do not want them to worry / think I am not capable', avoiding explicit commitment to communicate with family.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to review past successful experiences to balance current negative cognition
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting positive facts as unrepresentative exceptions, to maintain the 'I am not good enough' self-schema
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using seemingly rational statements like 'that was just an exception, this time is different', flat tone with Self-doubt, to negate positive evidence.

manifestations: Withdrawing in front of classmates, reducing interaction
Hesitant to ask family for help; worrying about being a burden
outcomes: Reduced social support, further worsening academic difficulties

manifestations: Pessimistic about future job prospects, believing 'I may never find Work'
outcomes: A sense of despair and worsening pessimism

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Hesitating to seek support from family, internalizing stress and worry as self-blame
Withdrawing in front of peers, reducing direct interaction

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism like 'I am not smart enough/not good enough'
Worrying about 'making others worry / look down on me', being extra cautious in seeking help and interacting

exception_events.target_problem: When facing academic situations like assignments and exams, the client typically catastrophizes Anticipation, struggles to concentrate, and falls into Self-doubt and pessimism Around the time grades are published.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several past courses, despite initially expecting failure, the client ultimately achieved Good grades, different from the usual pessimistic Anticipation.
exception_events.reason: Different actions and support: adopted more effective Learning methods and once received academic support; task breakdown and pacing were better suited, making Anxiety bearable, so the outcome deviated.

positive_force: Family is generally supportive and can be a potential resource
Past successful experiences show the possibility of competence and growth
Willing to try new methods (open to behavioral experiments)
Has proactively improved study habits and sought academic support
negative_force: Catastrophizing, predicting the future, overgeneralization, and negating-the-positive cognitive distortions
Relationship tension with classmates limiting access to peer support
Rising stress from balancing academics with other responsibilities

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent worry and difficulty concentrating while studying
antecedent: Around the time grades are published
When receiving homework or exam feedback
The stage of preparing for exams and completing tasks
target_behavior.core_reason: One or several below-Anticipation grades triggered catastrophizing and failure-predicting cognitions, leading to Impaired concentration and sustained Anxiety.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of failure and judgment, trying to gain a subjective sense of control (through worry and Self-protection)
target_behavior.consequence: Further decline in Learning efficiency and grades, worsened Low mood, affected eating habits

target_behavior.behavior: Withdrawing in front of classmates, Avoids communication
antecedent: Scenarios of interacting with classmates or comparing academic performance
Post-class discussions and exchanging assignment feedback with peers
target_behavior.core_reason: Comparison-and-despair cognitive patterns and Low sense of self-worth, worrying about being looked down on or exposing inadequacy.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding social evaluation and shame, reducing Anxiety triggers
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, Reduced social support, further intensifying Academic pressure and negative emotions
